court: New York Supreme Court, Appellate Division
notes: A referee's factual finding recites that plaintiff 'rented furnished rooms, kept boarders' as part of household income during a long-term cohabitation, but the case's actual dispute (misjoinder of causes of action, unenforceability of a contract founded on immoral consideration, housekeeper compensation) has nothing to do with the legal character or regulation of lodging/boarding arrangements. Passing factual mention only.

Concerns criminal prosecution for operating a fat-rendering/fertilizer business under a statute prohibiting such businesses as public nuisances; no connection to lodging, boarding, or letting of dwelling rooms.

A use-and-occupation/implied-tenancy dispute over a factory building retained by a seller after conveyance; addresses landlord-tenant vs. licensee/bailee distinctions for commercial/industrial premises, not lodging or dwelling rooms let to boarders.

holding_summary: Plaintiff, who kept a boarding house, sued a physician defendant for breach of an oral agreement to occupy furnished rooms with board and attendance for a year; the Court of Appeals held that because defendant never pleaded the Statute of Frauds nor objected to the oral proof at trial, he could not raise the statute for the first time on a motion to dismiss, and affirmed the judgment for plaintiff based on the parol agreement as proved.

quotes.text: The complaint alleges that the plaintiff, in the month of October, 1887, was in the possession under a lease of a house in the city of Yew York, and that she entered into an agreement with the defendant whereby the defendant leased from her, for the term of one year from the first day of November, 1887, the two front rooms on the second floor, and the back parlor and extension room, with the use of the front parlor on the first floor, with board and attendance to be furnished during the time by the plaintiff for the defendant and his assist:ant or associate in business, for the sum of $3,250, payable in equal monthly payments of $270.83 in advance.

notes: characterization left null: the Court of Appeals expressly declined to resolve whether the arrangement (furnished rooms plus board and attendance, at a boarding house) was a lease or a boarding/lodging contract, disposing of the appeal solely on the pleading/Statute-of-Frauds waiver issue ('It is unnecessary to consider this question, as the conclusion reached with reference to the question of pleading is fatal to the appeal.'). Appellant's brief argued such contracts are not leases and cite Wilson v. Martin, but that is counsel's argument, not the court's holding, so it is not treated as a supporting quote for characterization.

Murder prosecution turning on deliberation/premeditation and evidentiary/charge errors; a single narrative reference to the deceased pointing out furnished rooms for a prospective marital home is incidental color, not a legal treatment of lodging or letting.

Concerns Fire Department authority to order removal/securing of combustible packing-box storage in a yard and whether the reasonableness of such an order is contestable in a penalty action; no bearing on lodging houses or letting of dwellings.

Addresses a steamboat company's liability, analogized to an innkeeper's, for money stolen from a passenger's locked stateroom, contrasted with sleeping-car companies. This is carrier/innkeeper tort liability for guest property, not a case about the legal character of a householder letting dwelling rooms or the regulation of boarding houses; outside the corpus's scope despite the innkeeper analogy.

A fixtures dispute between successive tenants of land over ownership of buildings erected by a former tenant; ordinary landlord-tenant fixtures law, no relation to lodging or short-term letting of dwellings.
Concerns construction of a reserved easement/right of way to a wood lot; a real property servitude case with no connection to lodging houses or letting of dwellings.

court: New York Court of Common Pleas
notes: General Term opinion in the same Adams v. New Jersey Steamboat Co. dispute over stateroom theft liability, comparing steamboat companies to innkeepers and distinguishing sleeping-car companies. Carrier/innkeeper property-loss liability, not a case addressing a householder's letting of dwelling rooms or boarding-house regulation.

Mandamus proceeding over the Brooklyn mayor's refusal to license a building for public athletic exhibitions (boxing, wrestling, etc.); a places-of-public-amusement licensing case with no connection to lodging or boarding houses.
Certiorari review of a liquor license refusal based on proximity to a church/school under the Excise Law; no connection to lodging or boarding house letting.

Ejectment/title dispute turning on tax-sale deeds and whether a daughter's continued residence (during which she and her mother 'kept boarders') gave a mortgagee constructive notice of an unrecorded deed. The boarding activity is cited only as ambiguous evidence of possession, not as the subject of any holding about lodging/letting law.

holding_summary: In a conversion action between plaintiff and defendant, the court held that the trial judge erred in refusing to charge that where a husband and wife live together and the wife keeps boarders in the house, the husband -- not the wife -- is entitled to the board money paid by the boarders, absent a special agreement between the spouses giving the wife that money as her sole property.

quotes.text: Where a husband and wife live together and the wife keeps boarders in the house, the husband is entitled to the board money, unless a special agreement between the husband and wife allowing her to have it for her sole property is shown.

notes: Only tangential dispute here is intramarital ownership of boarding proceeds, not the legal character of the letting itself vis-a-vis the boarders; the court treats a wife's keeping of boarders in the family home as an unremarkable, lawful domestic economic activity (a favorable, ordinary-incident-of-household treatment), which is why it is marked favorable despite the narrow marital-property holding. duration_of_occupancy is unclear -- no facts given about how long any boarder stayed.

court: New York Supreme Court, Appellate Term
notes: Ordinary residential/commercial apartment holdover-tenancy dispute (year-to-year lease of the upper part of a building); one cited authority (Haynes v. Aldrich) happened to involve a subtenant running a boarding house, but the case itself does not address lodging or boarding-house law.

A statute-of-limitations case about whether a debtor who traveled and stayed abroad for his son's health 'resided without the state' so as to toll the statute; no connection to lodging or letting of dwellings despite the 'sojourner' selector match.

Concerns the Brooklyn mayor's lack of power to revoke a theatre/place-of-public-amusement license without common council authorization; a public-amusement licensing/police-power case unrelated to lodging or boarding houses.

court: New York Supreme Court, Appellate Term
notes: A bank-check dishonor/pleading case about anticipatory breach; it merely cites Crane v. Powell in passing as authority for the rule that a boarding-house keeper need not tender performance after a boarder repudiates. No independent treatment of lodging or letting law.
